strengths: Addresses genuine problem of poor cross-dataset generalization in SOD through practical synthetic data approach
Creates large-scale high-quality synthetic dataset (139,981 images, 2x+ larger than existing SOD datasets combined) with demonstrated quality control
Strong empirical results with 20-30% MAE improvements in cross-dataset generalization and state-of-the-art performance across 7 benchmarks
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including extensive ablations (Tables 5-8) that validate each component and design choice
Thoughtful integration of multiple techniques: multi-modal diffusion, iterative feedback-driven generation, multi-stage quality filtering, and ambiguity-aware architecture
Thorough evaluation methodology with appropriate metrics for SOD and attention to reproducibility details
Effectively demonstrates that synthetic data training can match or exceed task-specific model performance
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty—mostly applies existing techniques (FLUX-DIT diffusion, DINO-v3 features, standard losses) with straightforward engineering rather than novel algorithmic contributions

Ambiguity-aware architecture central to contributions but insufficiently analyzed: unclear how often genuine ambiguity occurs vs. model uncertainty, what percentage of scenes need multi-masks, how masks are selected at inference, minimal ablation impact (Table 7)
Critical hyperparameter choices (λ_mask=10, λ_score=0.05, λ_reg=0.1, γ=0.2, ψ=0.8, β=0.5) lack justification and sensitivity analysis
Shallow dataset quality assessment: only 0.7% manually verified with suspiciously low defect rates (14 incomplete masks in 1,000 samples); no inter-annotator agreement or rigorous domain gap analysis

Missing computational cost analysis: iterative generation pipeline cost not discussed, inference time comparisons absent, S3OD has ~117M parameters (substantially more than some baselines) but efficiency trade-offs not addressed

Experimental design issues: no statistical significance testing, error bars, or confidence intervals; baseline models from different years (2019-2024); unclear capacity control across compared models; oracle evaluation somewhat unrealistic
No failure case analysis or identification of remaining limitations; missing discussion of edge cases and method failure modes
Insufficient comparison with recent synthetic SOD methods (MaskFactory, DatasetDM comparisons incomplete; missing head-to-head with other generative approaches)
Generalization scope limited to natural images with specific objects; no testing on out-of-distribution domains (medical, microscopy, thermal); unclear robustness to significant distribution shifts
Missing ablations on quality filtering components and their individual contributions; limited analysis of which filtering stages remove what percentage of samples

strengths: Large-scale synthetic SOD dataset (139K+ images) substantially larger than existing datasets, will have significant practical value for the community
Comprehensive experimental validation across 6 benchmarks with strong cross-dataset generalization results (20-50% error reduction) and convincing zero-shot transfer to camouflaged object detection

Well-engineered multi-modal diffusion pipeline effectively combining FLUX DIT, DINO-v3, and concept attention for high-quality synthesis with rigorous 6-stage quality filtering achieving 6.8% rejection rate
Strong empirical results showing models trained only on synthetic data achieve competitive or superior performance to those trained on real data, with state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks
Rigorous quality control with Gemma-3 VLM assessment, semantic validation, and consistency filtering demonstrating higher quality than MaskFactory and other synthetic datasets
Good reproducibility documentation including implementation details, training time, computational requirements, and thoughtful ablation studies on architecture components and iterative generation
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty - primarily combines existing techniques (FLUX, DINO-v3, multi-choice learning) without introducing new losses, architectures, or algorithms; individual components are straightforward applications of prior work

Insufficient analysis of synthetic-to-real domain gap and reasons for effectiveness - lacks systematic study of which object categories/scene types generalize better, failure modes, or deep insights into why synthetic data outperforms expectations

Iterative generation mechanism may introduce bias toward specific object categories through category weight adaptation; parameters (α=8, β=0.5) appear arbitrary without sensitivity analysis or justification

Incomplete baseline comparisons under identical training conditions - many baseline results sourced from prior works with potentially different setups; limited comparison with other recent synthetic data generation methods and domain adaptation techniques

Missing critical ablations - no study of dataset size vs quality trade-offs, sensitivity to LLM prompts, necessity of individual diffusion model components, or justification for selecting specific FLUX layers [4,16,27,38]

Evaluation protocol concerns - baseline methods may not be retrained on identical datasets; risk of overfitting to benchmark characteristics used for iterative adaptation; zero-shot camouflaged object detection uses ground-truth real image masks

S3OD provides no train/test split since fully synthetic, limiting certain research directions; dataset release timing unclear; code availability stated as future work; potential biases from LLM prompts not analyzed

Incomplete technical justification - multi-mask decoder design lacks thorough motivation for SOD specifically; exponential decay weighting in loss function not clearly justified; smallest gains on DAVIS-S (Table 4) suggest domain-specific limitations
